![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/ebb0b09ffab6ffdff6a04104b09d6904302fdb7580262663b5e0c65bd3f95502.png)

The region $D$ is enclosed by the the curve $y=(x-1)^{2}$ and the lines $y=x+1$ and $y=3-x,$ as shown in the picture. Evaluate ${∬}_{D}2y\,dA.$
questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/f26c3e1bbbc268308db8d419bc799ad5349673e97c8828471997a5d36cb94d7d.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,(x-1)^{2}\le y\le x+1\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,(x-1)^{2}\le y\le 3-x\}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{x+1}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{3-x}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{|}_{(x-1)^{2}}^{x+1}\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}{|}_{(x-1)^{2}}^{3-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(x+1)^{2}-(x-1)^{4}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}[(3-x)^{2}-(x-1)^{4}]\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1}+{[-\frac{(3-x)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{5}}{5}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =((\frac{8}{3}-0)-(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}))+((-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})-(-\frac{8}{3}-0)) \\  & =\frac{32}{15}+\frac{32}{15} \\  & =\frac{64}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=2x,$ $y=5-3x$ and $x=0.$
Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2} \\ y=5-3x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{5-y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/805f6d6117e6c9028cb63f1ff8328bc625dc992a1f270abecdf898df31204613.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/b394a5a80ab4fafdcc7e5457f37360d693ddb7c24e1f6ed208ada3b778b3623c.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le x\le \frac{y}{2}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le y\le 5,\,0\le x\le \frac{5-y}{3}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{(5-y)/3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4},$ and the lines $y=5-2x$ and $y=-\frac{x}{3}.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & \,⟹\,x=2\sqrt{y} \\ y=5-2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{5}{2}-\frac{y}{2} \\ y=-\frac{x}{3} & \,⟹\,x=-3y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/b0f6f95d81c665d189d1b1e97f78b82b6c64abd5c1ae17ffe4f918e7650a7bcc.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/873c2a14782c1ceb96fc3c1c71888dd221761d21749824e39157671979a62f0f.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,-3y\le x\le \frac{5}{2}-\frac{y}{2}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,2\sqrt{y}\le x\le \frac{5}{2}-\frac{y}{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-3y}^{5/2-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2\sqrt{y}}^{5/2-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}12x\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14161415/assets/0e69b1cb480b87216273db4336adff57cbf9d9bc450aac4b0cdb58b1ae63f6f7.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 0,\,-\frac{2x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\frac{4x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}12x\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}12x\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}12x\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{-2x/3}^{x/3+3}12x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{4x/3}^{x/3+3}12x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}12xy\,{|}_{-2x/3}^{x/3+3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}12xy\,{|}_{4x/3}^{x/3+3}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}12x[\frac{x}{3}+3+\frac{2x}{3}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}12x[\frac{x}{3}+3-\frac{4x}{3}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}12x(x+3)\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}12x(3-x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}(12{x}^{2}+36x)\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}(36x-12{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =(4{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}){|}_{-3}^{0}+(18{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}){|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =-(4(-3)^{3}+18(-3)^{2})+18(3)^{2}-4(3)^{3} \\  & =108-162+162-108 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
